summary: Requires colleges participating in federal student aid programs to annually email and post in handbooks, orientations, health centers, and websites a list of campus and community resources, available accommodations, and Title IX complaint procedures for students who are or may become pregnant and choose to carry the baby to term.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Higher Education Act to require information dissemination by participating institutions but creates no new programs, funding streams, or expenditures. It has no bearing on government spending levels.
No provisions address taxes, tax rates, or revenue measures of any kind.

The bill concerns accommodations and resources at higher-education institutions for pregnant students but does not alter healthcare delivery systems, coverage models, or public versus private healthcare policy.
No provisions relate to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions address immigration, visas, border policy, or pathways to citizenship.

The bill repeatedly emphasizes resources and protections to help students 'carry a baby to term,' requires dissemination of information supporting that choice, and strengthens Title IX complaint processes for students facing discrimination because of a decision to carry to term. This directly advances a policy orientation that favors continuation of pregnancy over termination.
No provisions concern military or defense spending.
No provisions relate to environmental regulations or climate policy.
The bill mentions campus and community resources for pregnant students but does not expand or contract federal welfare programs such as SNAP, TANF, or Medicaid.

The bill adds a federal mandate under the Higher Education Act requiring institutions to disseminate specific information on pregnant-student rights and accommodations. This modestly increases federal involvement in higher-education administration.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related criminal penalties.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal-justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
No provisions address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No provisions address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions address foreign aid.
No provisions address voting access or election procedures.
No provisions address technology regulation or data privacy.
No provisions address worker protections or union rights.
The bill references Title IX enforcement but does not create or modify religious exemptions or balance religious liberty against anti-discrimination rules.
